title: How Indian courts actually apply the polluter pays principle
p1:
A company pollutes a river. Who pays for the damage?

Many assume the answer is simply a fine imposed by the government. But Indian courts have taken a much broader view of the polluter pays principle.
p2:
The surprising part: courts do not treat pollution as just a violation of rules. They can make polluters pay for restoring the environment itself.

This means the cost of cleaning contaminated water, repairing ecological damage, or compensating affected communities can be placed on the person or company responsible.
p3:
The Supreme Court has repeatedly applied this principle to ensure that businesses cannot profit from activities while leaving society to bear the environmental cost.

The idea is simple: those who create environmental harm must take responsibility for fixing it.

For companies, this is more than a legal issue. Environmental compliance is becoming a core part of responsible business practices.

A cleaner environment is not just a government duty; it is a shared responsibility backed by law.
conclusion: Do you think companies causing environmental damage should pay only penalties, or should they fully fund restoration of the damage they create?
